advisories.title: The tightened citationDiscipline says live pins are recorded 'nowhere else', but whatThisDoesNotDo[1] also records live pins
advisories.detail: The repair to my V10-A2 fixed the universal quantifier and, in the same sentence, strengthened exclusivity from v10's 'recorded only at reMeasurementAtVN' to 'recorded only at reMeasurementAtVN and nowhere else'. Read across the document that is contradicted by the artifact's own content: whatThisDoesNotDo[1] carries four live digests - corpus v1, its two REJECT verdicts, and corpus v2 - and corpus v2's live pin is additionally recorded at reMeasurementAtV10, so it appears in two places. The duplication is benign and I verified both instances against live bytes and they agree at 70248781.... The clause's evident scope is bindingSources whole-document digests, which is what the preceding sentence establishes, and forbidding the whatThisDoesNotDo citations would contradict a landed repair that both reviewers asked for. Scoping the sentence to bindingSources would remove the tension.
advisories.notBlocking: No pin is wrong, the duplicated value is consistent, and the clause's purpose - keeping later-authoring claims out of bindingSources - is satisfied.

advisories.title: The CLAUDE-V10-S2 entry describes the idCollisionNote change as an AMEND when it is an ADD
advisories.detail: The operation reads 'AMEND /appliesFindingsOf/idCollisionNote'. That key does not exist in v10 - v10 carried a differently-scoped note inside /appliesFindingsOf/codexV9 - so the v11 change is an addition, and my diff records it as ADDED. Elsewhere this artifact is careful about the verb, using ADD for new keys (ADD /appliesFindingsOf/notFoldedThisSuccessor in the sibling entry, ADD /sources/reMeasurementAtV10 at v10) and AMEND for edits. Since the repairLog is the audit instrument a later reviewer walks path by path, the verb is worth keeping accurate.
advisories.notBlocking: The path is named, so the completeness claim holds and I verified it; only the verb is imprecise.
